Even Apple CEO Tim Cook has admitted that Vision Pro is a niche product. I have said in the past that this device is a necessary step on the path towards a more affordable, consumer-friendly pair of Apple Glasses.

But at the same time, it's worth noting that niche products can sometimes have a major impact in professional fields, and a new surgical study clearly illustrates why it matters just as much to patients as it does to surgeons...

Vision Pro's surgical applications are growing

Endoscopic surgery involves sending small instruments into the body through a thin tube, with surgeons operating by watching the camera feed on a screen in the operating room. This approach requires much smaller incisions, which can dramatically shorten patients' recovery time.

Many surgeons have already replaced the traditional screen with the Vision Pro headset. The earliest known case dates back more than two years ago, when a renowned neurosurgeon used it to perform several spinal reconstruction procedures. Other doctors have also said that the device can reduce pain and discomfort for surgeons, and even lower their risk of injury.

The headset has also been used by other members of the surgical team, including a veteran scrub nurse who said the device allowed them to accurately anticipate the tools the surgeon would need next, eliminating the possibility of human error.

The device has also been used to help surgeons plan and preview procedures before they are carried out by surgical robots, and to assist with visualisation during conventional surgery as well.

While the US$3,500 price tag is steep for the average consumer, it is actually very cheap compared with the traditional screens used in operating rooms, which cost around US$20,000 each.

"Faster and better"

Analyst Horace Dediu was involved in a peer-reviewed study conducted by the University of California, San Diego, that demonstrated the value of Vision Pro for surgeons. The study found that swapping the traditional screen for the Vision Pro headset could deliver a range of benefits for surgeons and patients alike.

The study compared procedures performed using a traditional screen with those performed using Vision Pro, and found advantages across multiple areas.

• Surgical time was reduced by 19% • Functional success rate reached 100%, with no complications either during or after surgery • Surgeons' self-reported workload was significantly lower, and all surgeons involved in the study preferred the Vision Pro experience • Ergonomics improved, allowing surgeons to maintain a natural, forward-facing posture

So Vision Pro is a developmental tool that helps Apple pave the way for a true consumer product — but in the right hands, it already offers significant value in its own right.
